text:
maya: proposing a 'slab' fallback strategy for canaries — thinking of grouping model-variant + region as a single fallback unit instead of only model-level or region-level fallbacks. opening short RFC if folks +1 or have objections

ashwin: what exactly is a slab vs the current lane/fallbacks? quick TL;DR pls

maya: slab = {model variant, region, capacity tier}. idea: fallback a slab (route out of that entire chunk) when joint signals indicate it's unhealthy, rather than toggling just the model or just the region. avoids repeated oscillation where model is fine in region A but not B and we flip model and region separately

taylor: worried about A/B experiments. if we pull a slab we might bias tests. do we keep canary sample sticky so experiment integrity remains?

maya: good call. plan is sticky sampling by user cookie/consumer id for experiment window, but allow traffic rebalancing to preserve global RPS. fallback removes the slab from routing table but we keep experiment assignment metadata so cohorts remain balanced across remaining slabs

zheng: what signals trigger slab eviction? errors only? or latency/capacity too? need sensible defaults + backoff

ashwin: propose multi-signal heuristic: 1) error rate 3x baseline sustained for T_window; 2) p95 latency > 2x baseline AND queueing > 200ms; 3) capacity pressure: GPU free < 30% and queue length increasing. combine with :majority vote: at least two signals before eviction

maya: draft config snippet below (for runtime and console UX). open to naming suggestions for 'slab_eviction_policy'.

```yaml
slab_eviction_policy:
  enabled: true
  min_canary_pct: 1
  signals:
    errors:
      multiplier_threshold: 3.0
      window_seconds: 60
    latency:
      p95_multiplier: 2.0
      window_seconds: 60
    capacity:
      gpu_free_pct_threshold: 30
      avg_queue_ms_threshold: 200
  required_signal_count: 2
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  rollback_action: fallback_to_variant: stable
```

release-bot: deploy v0.40.2 started for rollout/experiment-17 — canary=5% in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 :rocket:

ops-bot: alert: us-east-1 slab-3 queue_ms rising to 520ms over last 2m (instances scaling) :eyes:

ashwin: when ops-bot fires, do we immediately mark capacity signal or wait for other signals? we should avoid noisy single-signal evictions during autoscale spikes

maya: plan: capacity signal is considered "soft" — counts as half a vote. combined with one hard signal (errors or latency) reaches required_signal_count. that avoids single-signal action during transient autoscale. also cooldown prevents flipflop

taylor: on the console side, we should show a projected traffic split if a slab is evicted (preflight): current->projected so PMs understand experiment impact. plus Undo button to re-add slab with reason note

ashwin: agree. also add a telemetry tag to every request routed during a rollback window so we can compute bias/regression metrics post-eviction (important for A/B causality)

zheng: what about region-only failure modes (network partition to region)? should we favor regional failover before slab-level if model works elsewhere? e.g., if only region connectivity is bad, don't evict model variants globally

maya: we can encode priority: region-only signals -> region-failover (remove region's slabs for that model); model-only signals -> model-variant fallback; joint signals -> slab eviction. default policy: try narrower scope first, escalate to slab if narrower fixes don't help within escalation_window_seconds

ashwin: propose escalation_window_seconds = 120 and max_escalation_steps = 2. Also record decision graph events to telemetry so we can audit why a slab was evicted

taylor: UI wishlist: 1) per-rollout decision timeline 2) live simulated traffic after each eviction 3) instant replay of routed requests for the cohort 4) a "safety leash" toggle for experiments that disables auto-evict

maya: love that. safety_leash will default ON for all A/B experiments but OFF for infra-only rollouts. need to wire through RBAC so only leads can disable

zheng: one more thing — quotas. if fallback increases pressure on stable pool, should we throttle fallback rate to avoid thrashing? e.g., only allow 1 slab eviction per 60s per region

ashwin: yes, slab eviction rate-limiter is needed. add global and per-region tokens. also prefer fallback to cheaper quantized variants before full stable fallback if model quality rules allow :sparkles:

maya: next steps: I'll spin up a short RFC doc with config proposal + console mocks + telemetry events list. want to land default heuristics and cooldowns before we wire autoscale signals. tagging @taylor @ashwin @zheng for review, will ping eng-telemetry next for event schema

ashwin: +1, please include sample Grafana queries for p95/queue/e2e errors

ops-bot: noted — created incident stub #IR-2024-125 for monitoring playbook updates

maya: thanks all. I'll post RFC link shortly. (reacts :thumbsup:)
